hints.content:
The number lines show that the ratio of $\maroonD{\text{kilometers}}$ to $\blueE{\text{percentage}}$ is $\maroonD{48}:\blueE{100\%}$.

We are looking for ratios that are equivalent to $\maroonD{48}:\blueE{100\%}$.

$\maroonD{48}\div12= \purpleE4$

So, we can find the percentage for $12\,\text{km}$ by dividing both parts of the ratio by $\purpleE{4}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{25\%}$ of $48$ is $\maroonD{12}$.

options.alt: A double number line with 3 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Distance, kilometers, reads from left to right: 0, 12, 48. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 25 percent, 100 percent. An arrow from the pair 48 to 100 percent to the pair 12 to 25 percent is labeled divided by 4.

hints.content:
$\maroonD{60}\div\maroonD{12}=\purpleE{5}$

Now we can find the percentage for $\maroonD{60\,\text{km}}$ by multiplying both parts of the new ratio by $\purpleE{5}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{125\%}$ of $48$ is $\maroonD{60}$.

This makes sense because $60\,\text{km}$ is farther than $48\,\text{km}$. So it should be more than $100\%$ of the distance.

options.alt: A double number line with 4 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Distance, kilometers, reads from left to right: 0, 12, 48, 60. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 25 percent, 100 percent, 125 percent. An arrow from the pair 12 to 25 percent to the pair 60 to 125 percent is labeled times 5.
